Correct a weighted scatter for its downweighting, to first order, at the Gaussian model

Source: R/imputeCellGLoc.R
dot-gloc_correct_scatter.Rd

Dividing the whole matrix by kappa is correct only when the columns are independent. The weights are functions of the conditional residual. Write \(Z_k\) for the standardised conditional residual of cell \(k\); it is proportional to \((\Sigma^{-1}(x - \mu))_k\), and \(\mathrm{Cov}(x, \Sigma^{-1}(x - \mu)) = I\), so under the Gaussian model \(Z_k\) is independent of every other cell \(x_j\). A weight \(w(Z_k)\) therefore deflates cell \(k\)'s own second moment and leaves its cross-moments with the other cells unbiased to first order.

.gloc_correct_scatter(S_raw, kappa)

Arguments

S_raw

the uncorrected weighted scatter.

kappa

the scalar consistency factor from .gloc_consistency, \(E[w(Z) Z^2] / E[w(Z)]\) for \(Z \sim N(0, 1)\).

Value

the corrected scatter, with the dimnames of S_raw. A kappa of 1 or more, or a non-finite one, returns S_raw; a single column returns S_raw / kappa; if a Cholesky factorisation fails during the iteration, the symmetric correction .gloc_correct_scatter_sym(S_raw, kappa) is returned.

Details

The residual splits as \(R_k = m_k + s_k Z_k\) with the predictable part \(m_k\) independent of \(Z_k\), the weight downweights only the \(s_k Z_k\) part, and

$$E[w R_k^2] / E[w] = (\sigma_k^2 - s_k^2) + \kappa s_k^2,$$

where \(s_k^2 = 1 / (\Sigma^{-1})_{kk}\) is the conditional variance. The correction therefore adds the missing part to the diagonal and keeps the raw off-diagonals:

$$\Sigma = \Sigma_{raw} + (1 - \kappa)\, \mathrm{diag}(s_k^2(\Sigma)).$$

Because \(s_k^2\) depends on \(\Sigma\), the equation is solved by fixed-point iteration, starting from \(\Sigma_{raw}\) with its diagonal divided by \(\kappa\), for at most 200 steps, stopping at a relative change below 1e-12. The result is positive definite whenever \(\Sigma_{raw}\) is, since a positive diagonal is added. Under independence it reduces to \(\Sigma_{raw} / \kappa\), and with no downweighting to \(\Sigma_{raw}\).

The correction is first order, not exact. The raw covariances are themselves about 2.5% low (0.683 for a true 0.700 at n = 10000): several weights in one row interact, and cellWise::cwLocScat imputes the downweighted fraction with its own scatter. The correction therefore over-corrects slightly. Measured on clean data (five variables at correlation 0.7, a sixth at 0.1 to all, design ~ ., n = 10000, three replicates), against the symmetric rescaling it replaced (see .gloc_correct_scatter_sym): conditional variances 1.045 of the truth (0.866 before), block correlation 0.682 (0.742 before; truth 0.700), marginal variances 0.996 (0.978), cells with \(W < 0.5\) 0.99% (1.86%; nominal 1.12%), and 15 against 26 iterations. A correlation bias of about -0.02 therefore remains. On the pilot grid of the categorical EM (900 paired fits, only this function differing) the default arm's categorical hit rate rose by 0.011 and its detection AUC by 0.006, its imputation MSE fell by 3.6%, its false flags in complete rows fell from 2.33% to 1.21%, and it took 0.59 times the time.
